clue.text: It puts Frenchman out of his misery

definitions.text: It puts Frenchman out of his misery

parts.words: It puts Frenchman out of his misery
parts.note: read as a mercy killing described in French terms: the final blow that ends suffering, named with a French phrase

explanation.definitionFit: The French term for a finishing blow is used for any act that puts a sufferer out of their misery.

clue.text: No longer popular fashion causes fury

parts.note: something no longer popular is out
the rage is the current fashion, as in all the rage

explanation.surface: Something that has gone out of style makes people angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is intense anger, a synonym of fury.

clue.text: China-no replica can be made

indicators.note: the letters of the fodder can be made into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that no copy of some fine china can be produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' hides behind its capital at the start; it is the crockery, not the country. 'can be made' rearranges NO REPLICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine china is the everyday name for this ceramic ware.

clue.text: Days in church when monarch accepts medal

indicators.note: the monarch takes in the medal, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Church holy days on which the sovereign receives a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: Ember days are seasonal fasting days in the church calendar; the definition reads 'Days' with the answer as their name. The MBE is a British honour given by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ember days are four sets of fasting and prayer days in the Christian liturgical year.

clue.text: Performance reviewed in article

indicators.note: viewed again, re-viewed, suggests the letters of article are looked over and reordered

explanation.surface: A concert critiqued in a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' sounds like a critic's job, which suits a performance, but it rearranges ARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical or poetry performance, often by one soloist.

clue.text: Care what police may give offender

definitions.meaning: care in the sense of wariness or prudence
a formal warning issued by police instead of a charge

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both prudence and the formal warning police give a minor offender.

clue.text: Return piece to one's opposite number

parts.note: to counter is to return a blow or argument
a part is a piece of something

explanation.surface: Giving a chess piece back to the person playing against you.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterpart is the person holding the equivalent role on the other side.

clue.text: Declined to make note in a bad case

indicators.note: the words a bad act as a case enclosing the note

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone refused to write a memo while in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declined' looks like refused, but here it means lessened. 'case' makes A BAD hold TE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abated means diminished or subsided, as a storm declines in strength.

clue.text: One going round hav, ing gold tooth

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a biter is a jocular word for a tooth

explanation.surface: Someone circling about with a gold tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbiter is a spacecraft or body that travels in a circuit around a planet.

clue.text: Support that the irritating get?

definitions.meaning: a reserve or reinforcement held ready
irritating people get your ..., as the idiom says

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a reserve or standby, and irritating people are said to get your back up.

clue.text: Given saturation coverage

parts.note: media jargon for blanket reporting, read literally as being covered with water until soaked

explanation.definitionFit: Ground or wood soaked through with water has been literally saturated.

clue.text: Fool introduces charge for fertiliser

parts.note: a nit is a fool or idiot
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: An idiot sets the price for plant food.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrates are nitrogen compounds widely spread on fields as fertiliser.

clue.text: Wine turning nastier

indicators.note: the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Wine going off and getting worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' fits wine going sour, but it rearranges NASTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Provide with part of Carmen duet

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Supplying a portion of a duet from Bizet's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or supply someone with a quality.

clue.text: One could be very sick in this vehicle

definitions.text: One could be very sick in this vehicle

parts.words: One could be very sick in this vehicle
parts.note: sounds like travel sickness, but very sick means seriously ill, as a patient carried to hospital

explanation.definitionFit: Seriously ill patients are transported to hospital in this emergency vehicle.

clue.text: Don't gain from period of rest and calm

parts.note: a break is a pause or rest period
even means calm and steady, as an even temper

explanation.surface: Taking a holiday and staying placid brings no profit.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish with neither profit nor loss is to make no gain.

clue.text: Fish can struggle with energy, maybe

parts.note: a perch is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: the letters of can struggle into a new order

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A fish might fight in a tin, given enough vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchance is an old-fashioned word for perhaps.

clue.text: King's obsession about old country

indicators.note: the king and the obsession go about, around, the letter for old

parts.note: R is Rex, Latin for king
a mania is an obsession

explanation.surface: A ruler's fixation with his former homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a nation in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Made one's pile, not trusting the future?

definitions.text: Made one's pile, not trusting the future?

parts.words: Made one's pile, not trusting the future?
parts.note: making a pile sounds like getting rich, but here it is stockpiling against bad times to come

explanation.definitionFit: Someone wary of the future stores up a secret stock of goods or money.

clue.text: Legal to be executed? That's terrible

indicators.note: execution here is beheading, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: lawful means legal

explanation.surface: A grim joke: if killing is permitted, that is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' looks like carried out, but it means beheaded: LAWFUL loses its head, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful is a common synonym for dreadful or very bad.

clue.text: Summed up, keeping nothing secret

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in total and, read literally, having told everything.

clue.text: Conflict I'd interrupt for twenty-four hours

indicators.note: I'd breaks into the word for conflict, so it goes inside

parts.note: a fray is a fight or conflict

explanation.surface: A row broken off by someone for a whole day.
explanation.definitionFit: Friday is one day of the week, a span of twenty-four hours.

clue.text: Swindle worker-it's very prevalent

parts.note: a ramp is British slang for a swindle or racket
an ant is the classic crossword worker, from worker ants

explanation.surface: A con against a labourer is widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampant means spreading unchecked, so widespread and rife.

clue.text: Time to introduce sue-cesser of those people

parts.note: an heir is a successor

explanation.surface: The moment comes to present the next in line of a family.
explanation.definitionFit: Their is the possessive meaning belonging to them.

clue.text: Causing death: is that very funny?

definitions.meaning: hilarious, as in a comedy that is a scream

explanation.definitionFit: The word means slaying and also hilarious.

clue.text: Nervous, as boundary fielder is

definitions.meaning: in cricket a boundary fielder stands at the rim of the playing field

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means tense, and a cricket fielder on the boundary stands literally at the rim of the field.

clue.text: Abuse instrument before note made

indicators.note: the instrument comes before the note in the answer

parts.note: the viola is a stringed instrument
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Misusing a musical instrument before a note is produced.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate is to abuse or desecrate something.

clue.text: Pass terrible danger-point to explosive

parts.note: to hand is to pass something over

indicators.note: the letters of danger are terribly mangled into another order

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Handing over something horribly dangerous to a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand.
